clue.text: Play, since it gives solver pleasure

parts.note: 'as' can mean since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'
the solver is 'you', so something giving the solver pleasure is something you like

explanation.surface: A reviewer recommends a play on the grounds that the person reading will enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossword addresses the solver as 'you', so the second half reads as YOU LIKE IT; AS YOU LIKE IT is Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote this pastoral comedy set in the Forest of Arden, so it is an example of a stage work.

clue.text: Bogus, rubbish actor succeeded at first

indicators.note: 'at first' keeps only the first letter of 'succeeded'

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, placed at the start
a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor

explanation.surface: A bogus, terrible actor nonetheless managed to succeed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: S for succeeded is a genealogy abbreviation; 'at first' puts it before the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is something fake or counterfeit, so it works as an adjective for false.

clue.text: Curse when reluctant to go topless

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so losing the top removes it

parts.note: loath means unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone swears when unwilling to strip off their top.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a profane exclamation as well as a solemn promise, so it means a swear word.

clue.text: Barely moving at sea — fibbing as well, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this tells us to listen rather than read, so a phrase pronounced the same is wanted

parts.note: fibbing is lying, and as well is too

explanation.surface: A sailor claims his ship is hardly moving and is fibbing about it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship lying to is stopped with its head to the wind, holding position with little headway.

clue.text: Clark County?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the surname of Clark, Superman's alter ego at the Daily Planet
second meaning: a county in south-east England

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a US county named Clark, but the first word asks for Superman's surname and the second for an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman's civilian identity is Clark Kent, and Kent is the English county known as the Garden of England.

clue.text: Gently boils headless English duck

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter is cut off

parts.note: to simmer is to cook just below boiling
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A cook gently boils a decapitated English duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird in the pot, but it is the verb meaning to dunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to push them under water, which is to submerge them.

clue.text: BA's lounge? My poor kids were filmed causing mayhem in it!

definitions.text: kids were filmed causing mayhem in it

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the preceding letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

parts.note: these words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that children ran riot on video in the British Airways lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: The film's cast was entirely children, playing gangsters whose shootouts use custard-pie 'splurge guns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Parker's 1976 musical gangster film had a cast made up entirely of child actors creating chaos.

clue.text: Maybe Evelyn with segment on the radio for epic novel

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so words with the same pronunciation are wanted

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh is an example of someone with this surname, said like war in British English
with and and both join things
a segment is a piece of something

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast features a reading by Evelyn of a segment from an epic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh was a 20th-century English novelist; his surname is pronounced the same as war in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's War and Peace is a vast novel of the Napoleonic wars, the classic example of an epic.

clue.text: Fish doctor freed from frozen area

indicators.note: something freed from a place is no longer in it, so those letters come out

parts.note: the treeless frozen plain of the Arctic
standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A fish is thawed out by a doctor after being trapped in the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean-going food fish, so it is an example of the general category.

clue.text: Conservative area MP, Etonian, trained as a submariner

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or direct it, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory MP educated at Eton once served in the navy aboard submarines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained as' reads as a career history, but 'trained' is the anagram signal and 'as' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne's Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus, so he is literature's most famous submarine voyager.

clue.text: Heads of African states invest across the continent

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so each following word yields its front letter

parts.note: front letters of these three words
front letter of this word too

explanation.surface: African leaders put money into projects throughout the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' does double duty: its first letter completes the run, and it also points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents, so it fits a definition naming one.

clue.text: When touring Birmingham Lee — a bum — changed into a dandy

indicators.note: to tour is to go around something, so these letters surround another place
changing something alters its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
Brum is the informal name for Birmingham

explanation.surface: A layabout called Lee, visiting Birmingham, smartens himself up into a dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is England's second city, nicknamed Brum by its residents. Here the rearranged letters wrap around that nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Brummell was the Regency arbiter of men's fashion, the archetype of a fop or dandy.

clue.text: Legendary character Olaf Germany booted out?

indicators.note: something booted out is kicked about and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: these words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A legendary figure called Olaf is kicked out of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Morgan le Fay is the enchantress of Arthurian legend, half-sister of King Arthur.

clue.text: The Spanish back in Bilbao — clever — enunciate clearly

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine word for 'the'

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the closing letter of the Basque city's name
cute can mean shrewd or clever, as in 'a cute move'

explanation.surface: A Spaniard back home in Bilbao, being clever, speaks very distinctly.
explanation.definitionFit: To elocute is to speak in a formal, carefully articulated way, which is pronouncing words distinctly.

clue.text: Tennis player always tense

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tennis player is permanently nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Evert was an American champion who won eighteen Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: American fake news boss embarrassed

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a sham is a fake
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A US news chief is mortified over spreading fake news.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe feeling shame or awkwardness about something one has done.

clue.text: Stripped crossed laths in uppermost room

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer covering, so the end letters come away

parts.note: a lattice is a framework of crossed strips of wood

explanation.surface: Bare crisscrossed wooden strips are exposed in the top room of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the space or room directly under the roof, the highest in the house.

clue.text: Like an egg? Zero purchase tax, European

parts.note: the letter O looks like a zero
value added tax, the UK sales tax
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether eggs are free of purchase tax in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's tax added to the price of goods and services.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate is a botanical and descriptive term for egg-shaped, from Latin ovum, an egg.

clue.text: Sudden impulse has Patty getting undressed

indicators.note: undressing strips off the outer layers, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: a patty of minced meat is a burger

explanation.surface: Someone called Patty feels a sudden urge to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: Patty looks like a woman's name, but it is a meat patty, and a burger without its dressings loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong sudden desire to do something, which is what an impulse is.

clue.text: 20 Across is dull and boring, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this tells us the word is heard rather than read, so a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: slow can describe something tedious and dull

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a piece of fruit is dull and boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small blue-black fruit of the blackthorn, used to flavour gin.

clue.text: Healthy after eating starters of ripe unwaxed oranges?

indicators.note: something eating something else takes it inside, so the letters go within

parts.note: fit means in good health

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, so the two following words give their front letters

parts.note: the front letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Eating ripe, unwaxed oranges is suggested as the healthy option.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows that oranges are only an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are one kind of fruit, so the definition is an example of the category.

clue.text: Famous director collapsed at home on island

parts.note: fell means fell down
being in means being at home
I is the abbreviation for island, placed after

explanation.surface: A well-known film director collapsed at his island home.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was an Italian film director celebrated for La Dolce Vita and 8½.

clue.text: Area of hospital that sees plenty of drama?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the operating room where surgery is done
second meaning: a playhouse where plays are staged

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an emergency department full of drama, but the two halves name a surgical room and a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals have operating theatres for surgery, and a theatre is also the venue where plays are performed.

clue.text: Lock securing letter boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the answer sits inside the clue words

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A lock fastens the box that letters are posted into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a padlock and 'boxes' a postbox, but the lock is of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair, so it is a type of lock in the hairdressing sense.

clue.text: Lasting for ages, which can be deplorable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: persisting over a long time, as of an illness
second meaning: very bad, an informal British usage

explanation.surface: Something that drags on forever can become truly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: In everyday British speech the word also means dreadful, as in 'the food was chronic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically the word describes long-lasting conditions, and colloquially in Britain it means terrible or very poor.

clue.text: Mild-tempered maiden: "a mouse!"

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the cry someone gives on seeing a mouse

explanation.surface: A gentle young woman squeals on spotting a mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored, recorded as M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek describes someone quiet, gentle and submissive, which matches being of mild disposition.

clue.text: Monotonous Liberal article found in newspaper

indicators.note: something found in another thing is inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: the Financial Times
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dull article by a Liberal appears in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a British business daily printed on pink paper, abbreviated FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat describes a voice or delivery lacking variation or liveliness, just as monotonous does.

clue.text: Large sense of self? It's part of many people's childhood

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the ego is one's sense of self

explanation.surface: A big ego is something many people develop in childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the Danish interlocking plastic brick toy that most children have played with.

clue.text: Loud rage, passion

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A list of strong emotions: loud anger, passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is used figuratively for burning intensity of feeling, so it is a synonym of ardour.

clue.text: Outlaw killed, hit by rebels

indicators.note: here a verb: the letters rebel against their order and rise up into a new one

parts.note: these words supply the letters

explanation.surface: An outlaw was killed after being shot by rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy the Kid was a notorious Wild West gunman and outlaw, shot dead by Pat Garrett in 1881.

clue.text: Welsh chap's electronic commercial vehicle

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a van carries goods for business

explanation.surface: A Welshman owns an electric delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a common Welsh given name, the Welsh form of John, so it names a Welsh man.

clue.text: Classic novel one wouldn't associate with Amazon?

definitions.text: Classic novel one wouldn't associate with Amazon?

parts.words: Classic novel one wouldn't associate with Amazon?
parts.note: surface reading: a book you would not expect to find sold by the online retailer
setter's reading: the Amazons were a race of huge warrior women, so the opposite is women who are small

explanation.walkthrough: Amazon looks like the bookseller, but it is the mythical warrior woman; the novel's title names women who are anything but Amazonian.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott's 1868 book about the four March sisters is a classic American novel.
